settings.keyer.limits_note: The keyer never allows more than its own firmware limits.
settings.restart_note: Language change takes effect after restart.
wf.label: Waterfall
qso.title: Log QSO
qso.name: Name
qso.write_failed: Could not write the ADIF file: {msg}
tx.no_call: No callsign for {CALL} – click a callsign in the text or type it in the Call field.
cq.stopped_answer: CQ repeat stopped: someone is answering.
wavelog.queued: Wavelog: {pending} QSOs waiting to be sent
settings.wavelog.ok: Connection OK – address, API key and station profile accepted (test only, nothing was logged)
settings.macros.label: Button
rx.match.tip: Set my sending speed to the other station's speed
rx.info.tip: Speed, pitch and strength of the station being decoded. The pitch is the difference to your own sidetone, so 0 Hz means you are on the same frequency. The report is a suggestion from the measured signal-to-noise ratio in a 500 Hz bandwidth; check it before logging.
settings.keyer.winkeyer_note: K1EL WinKeyer or a compatible keyer (for example K3NG) at 1200 baud. Note: WinKeyer has no heartbeat, so if this program crashes the keyer sends the rest of its buffer (up to about a minute at 20 WPM). STOP, closing the window and losing the port all clear the buffer.
qrz.hint: Click a callsign in the text to look it up on QRZ.com.
qrz.no_login: Add your QRZ.com login in Settings to show name, QTH and locator here.
qrz.limited: Without a QRZ XML subscription QRZ.com gives only some of the fields.
qrz.f.name: Name
qrz.use.tip: Copy the name, QTH and locator into the QSO fields
qrz.web.tip: Open the callsign's page on qrz.com in the browser
qrz.used: QRZ.com details of {call} copied to the QSO
settings.qrz.auto: Look up the detected callsign automatically
settings.qrz.ok_limited: Login OK – no XML subscription, so only some fields are shown
settings.qrz.note: Uses the QRZ.com XML service. A free account gives name, town and country; an XML Logbook Data subscription also gives the locator, photo and QSL details. Without a login, clicking a callsign still offers the qrz.com web page. The password is stored in settings.json like the Wavelog key.
tx.tune.tip: Key down for {s} s for tuning the antenna (Ctrl+T). Click twice: the first click asks "Sure?", the second starts the carrier. While tuning, one click or Esc stops it.
tx.tune_busy: TUNE only when nothing is being sent.
settings.qso.worked.placeholder: optional ADIF file, e.g. an export from Wavelog
worked.new: New station – not in your log
update.restarting: Installing {version} – the program restarts in a moment.
update.wait_tx: Update after the transmission (and CQ repeat) has ended.
update.qso_open: The QSO with {call} has not been logged. Update and restart anyway?
update.why.source: Running from source code: update with git pull.
update.why.platform: One-click update is Windows only for now: download the new version and unpack it over the old one.
update.why.readonly: The program folder is not writable (for example in Program Files). Move it to e.g. C:\CWStation to update with one click.
update.why.no_checksum: The release has no checksum, so it is not installed automatically.
wavelog.duplicate: Wavelog: {call} was already in the log
wavelog.rejected: Wavelog refused the QSO with {call}: {msg}. It is kept in wavelog-rejected.jsonl in the settings folder; the other QSOs are sent normally.
